title: The 1960 'Magnetic Field Generator' That Cured Arthritis—Burned by AMA
hook: A device that healed chronic pain with magnetic fields was tested on thousands, then the American Medical Association ordered every prototype destroyed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines medical conspiracy with a tangible cure that was destroyed, tapping into distrust of medical institutions.

title: The 1928 'Death Ray' That Tesla Built—Then US Government Seized
hook: Nikola Tesla claimed his 'death ray' could destroy armies from 200 miles away—the FBI raided his lab and the plans vanished.
why_this_can_go_viral: Tesla is a viral magnet; the death ray legend is dark, mysterious, and suggests government suppression of superweapons.

title: The 1978 'Machine That Recycled 100% of Plastic'—Burned by Exxon
hook: A prototype that turned all plastic back into usable oil with zero emissions was purchased by Exxon executives and set on fire.
why_this_can_go_viral: Environmental anger meets corporate conspiracy—a perfect storm for viral outrage and shares.

title: The 1,600-Year-Old 'Greek Fire' Formula—Held by One Family, Then Lost
hook: Byzantine warships sprayed liquid fire that burned on water—the secret recipe was guarded by a single family and disappeared with their last member.
why_this_can_go_viral: Greek fire is a legendary mystery; the idea of a single family holding the key to a lost superweapon is gripping.

title: The 1954 'Cold Fusion Reactor' That Powered a Town—Then Vanished
hook: A small reactor in a rural Italian village provided free electricity for six months—then the military arrived and the inventor disappeared.
why_this_can_go_viral: Free energy and inventor disappearance is a high-trust conspiracy narrative; people love the 'they silenced him' story.

title: The 3,500-Year-Old 'Hittite Steel Sword' That Never Rusted—Lost Alloy
hook: Archaeologists found an iron sword that remained shiny after millennia underground—metallurgists say the alloy shouldn't exist.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'impossible metal' trope fascinates; the idea of ancient metallurgy surpassing modern science is a strong hook.

title: The 1903 'Airship That Flew Without Fuel'—Inventors Killed in Car Crash
hook: Two brothers built a dirigible that stayed aloft for days using only atmospheric electricity—they died in a one-car crash the night before their patent.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mysterious death before patent screams assassination; free energy airship is a dream many want to believe in.

title: The 1,200-Year-Old 'Chinese Machine Gun' That Fired 20 Arrows Per Second
hook: A crossbow mechanism from the Tang Dynasty could unleash a hail of arrows faster than any modern bow—the plans were burned by warlords.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ancient weapons that rival modern tech are always viral; the 'machine gun' angle is dramatic and visual.

title: The 1964 'Water-to-Fuel Converter'—NASA Classified It After Testing
hook: A lab technician accidentally created a device that split water into hydrogen fuel using almost no energy—NASA took it and sealed the file.
why_this_can_go_viral: Water-to-fuel is the ultimate dream; NASA classification adds a layer of dark conspiracy that drives shares.

title: The 5,500-Year-Old 'Sumerian Plow' That Planted Seeds Automatically
hook: A clay tablet shows a plow with a mechanical seed dispenser—the design was so advanced it wasn't rebuilt until the 1700s.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ancient automation challenges linear progress narratives; the 'rebuilt 1200 years later' fact is mind-blowing.

title: The 1931 'Mood Radio' That Made Listeners Euphoric—Destroyed by FCC
hook: A radio engineer built a transmitter that broadcast a frequency causing intense happiness—the FCC confiscated it and arrested him for 'disrupting public order.'
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a happiness device being banned tickles anti-authority instincts; perfect for conspiracy-minded viewers.

title: The 2,700-Year-Old 'Assyrian Battery' That Plated Gold—Lost Electrochemistry
hook: Assyrian artisans coated copper with gold using a method that required electricity—but no battery has ever been found from that era.
why_this_can_go_viral: The Baghdad battery controversy is evergreen; adding Assyrian gold plating deepens the mystery of ancient electricity.

title: The 1976 'Dream Learning Helmet'—US Army Sealed the Research
hook: A helmet that played lessons during REM sleep taught foreign languages in days—the Army tested it on soldiers, then classified every paper.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone wants to learn effortlessly; the idea that the military suppressed such a tool fuels outrage and curiosity.

title: The 1920 'Magnetic Engine' That Produced Free Energy—Inventor Poisoned
hook: John Worrell Keely demonstrated an engine that ran on 'vibratory force' for years—then he died of sudden paralysis after a meeting with oil magnates.
why_this_can_go_viral: The classic 'free energy inventor killed by big oil' story is endlessly viral; Keely is a deep-cut legend.

title: The 3,800-Year-Old 'Egyptian Lock' That Couldn't Be Picked—Until 2010
hook: A wooden lock from Pharaoh Senusret's tomb used a sliding pin system so complex that modern locksmiths couldn't open it for decades.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'ancient tech beats modern' trope always works; the lock mystery is tangible and visual.

title: The 1957 'Solar Furnace' That Melted Steel—Destroyed by Coal Lobby
hook: French engineer Félix Trombe built a solar reflector that reached 3,500°C—within months, coal industry lawyers had it dismantled.
why_this_can_go_viral: Clean energy destroyed by fossil fuel interests is a powerful narrative; the specific temperature and destruction detail sells it.

title: The 1,100-Year-Old 'Viking Compass' That Worked Under Clouds—Lost
hook: A wooden disk with mysterious crystals could find the sun even on overcast days—the last working one sank with a Viking ship in 1040.
why_this_can_go_viral: Viking navigation mystery is popular; the 'lost in shipwreck' angle adds tragic finality that drives curiosity.

title: The 1985 'Machine That Freshened Air in Cities'—Bought by BP
hook: A device that converted smog into breathable oxygen using a catalytic charge was purchased by BP—the patent vanished from every database.
why_this_can_go_viral: Pollution is a global anger point; a company burying a clean-air device is the ultimate villain story.

title: The 4,000-Year-Old 'Minoan Plumbing' That Ran Hot Water—Destroyed by Volcano
hook: The palace of Knossos had terracotta pipes that delivered heated water to baths—after the Thera eruption, the builders' secret died with them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ancient luxury like hot water surprises people; the volcanic destruction adds a dramatic end to a lost marvel.

title: The 1941 'Device That Made Tanks Invisible'—Tested, Then Sealed
hook: The British military tested a 'diffraction screen' that made a 30-ton tank disappear from radar and eyes—Winston Churchill ordered it destroyed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Invisibility tech is a universal fascination; Churchill's personal order to destroy it adds high-level conspiracy.

title: The 1972 'Pill That Reversed Aging'—Inventor Died Under Oath
hook: Biochemist Dr. Roy Walford developed a compound that extended mouse lifespan by 50%—he died of a heart attack while testifying to Congress.
why_this_can_go_viral: The desire for longevity is universal; a death during testimony screams foul play and fuels massive engagement.

title: The 3,200-Year-Old 'Egyptian Battery' Found in a Tomb—Still Producing Power
hook: A clay jar with copper and iron was discovered in 1938—when filled with ancient grape juice, it still generated measurable voltage.
why_this_can_go_viral: The Bagdad battery story is legendary; adding 'still working' and 'grape juice' makes it fresh and tactile.

title: The 1915 'Engine That Ran on Earth's Rotation'—Inventor Committed
hook: A self-taught physicist built a wheel that spun without external power—he was declared insane and institutionalized until his death.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'inventor silenced by mental asylum' story is dark, tragic, and suggests a cover-up—perfect viral fuel.

title: The 1961 'Light Bulb That Lasted 100 Years'—Bought and Buried by GE
hook: A scientist at GE developed a filament that showed no wear after 10 years—GE executives cancelled the project and destroyed all samples.
why_this_can_go_viral: The planned obsolescence conspiracy is already viral; the 100-year light bulb is the archetypal example that proves the theory.
